hints.title: Factorial Radix Digit Selection
hints.text: Fixing the first digit partitions all permutations into n blocks of size (n minus one) factorial. We can identify each digit directly via division.

hints.title: Zero-Based Index Quotient and Modulo
hints.text: Convert k to 0-based index by decrementing by one. The quotient k divided by (n minus one) factorial gives the index in the remaining available digits.

hints.title: Iterative Remainder Selection
hints.text: Remove the selected digit from available list, update k to k modulo factorial, decrement n, and repeat until all digits are placed.

hints.title: See the blueprint
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def getPermutation(self, n: int, k: int) -> str:
        nums = [str(i) for i in range(1, n + 1)]
        fact = 1
        for i in range(1, n):
            fact *= i
        k -= 1
        res = []
        for i in range(n - 1, 0, -1):
            idx = k // fact
            res.append(nums.pop(idx))
            k %= fact
            fact //= i
        res.append(nums[0])
        return "".join(res)
```

complexity.notes: Optimal solution achieving O(N^2) time and O(N) auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Generating all permutations sequentially via backtracking takes O(N!) time and exceeds runtime limits.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Factorial division directly selects each digit in O(N) steps with O(N) list removals.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should understand factorial number system (factoradics) and convert 1-based k to 0-based indexing.
